senses: purposeless, meaningless, worthless, useless, fruitless, empty, idle
la:adj:inanis.html:
ĭnānis, e, adj.
etym. dub.; cf. 2. in-
,
empty, void (opp. plenus; freq. and class.).
Physically: cum vas inane dicimus, non ita loquimur ut physici, quibus inane esse nihil placet, sed ita, ut verbi causa sine aqua, sine vino, sine oleo vas esse dicamus,: aqualis inanis (opp. plena),: tune inane quicquam putes esse, cum ita completa et conferta sint omnia, ut, etc.,: quae spatium pleno possint distinguere inane,: domum ejus exornatam et instructam, fere jam iste reddiderat nudam atque inanem,: granum inane cassumque,: quae (naves) inanes ad eum remitterentur,; so, naves (opp. onustae),; ; ; cf.: inde navigia inania et vacua hinc plena et onusta mittantur,: lagenae,: mensa,: vix incedo inanis, ne ire posse cum onere existimes,without a burden,; cf.: ego bajulabo: tu, ut decet dominum, ante me ito inanis,: janitor ad dantes vigilet: si pulset inanis Surdus, etc.,emptyhanded, without presents,hic homo est inanis,without money, without fortune,; ; : misera in civitate et inani,: egentes inanesque discedere,, § 25 fin.: structores ad frumentum profecti inanes redierunt,; cf. : equus,without a rider,; cf.: quid, quod omnes consulares ... simul atque assedisti partem istam subselliorum nudam atque inanem reliquerunt?: absint inani funere neniae,without a corpse,: parasitus,unfed, hungry,: venter,hungry,; cf.: siccus, inanis Sperne cibum vilem,: quod inani sufficit alvo,: laeva,without rings,: litterae,empty,: paleae,empty, light,: nubila,: venti,: tum ebur ex inani corpore extractum (a transl. of the Platon. ἀπολελοιπότος ψυχὴν σώματος), lifeless, dead, Mos.: corpus,; ; cf. in the foll.: vulgus,i. e. the shades,; cf. umbra,: imago,: regna Ditis,: Tartara,: leo, a lion's hide, ; so, tigris,: vultus,i. e. blind,: Gaurus, i. e. hollow (an extinct volcano), . —
With abl., gen., or ab (the last rare): nulla epistula inanis aliqua re utili,: Agyrinensis ager centum septuaginta aratoribus inanior est,: sanguinis atque animi pectus inane,: corpus animae,; ; (4, 17), 32: lymphae dolium,: pectus deorum,: inanis a marsupio, Prud. στεφ. 2, 104. —
Subst.: ĭnāne, is, n., an empty space, a void (most freq. in Lucr.): scilicet hoc id erit vacuum quod inane vocamus,: namque est in rebus inane,; cf. ; : ita nullum inane, nihil esse individuum potest,: plus esse inanis,: inani,: inane,; ; ; 514 et saep.: ad inane naturae,: per inane,through the air,; et saep.; ; ; et saep.—Abl.: inani,; : ab inani,: in inani,; : sine inani,; ; : per inania,; .
Trop.
In gen., empty, useless, worthless, vain, unprofitable: aures ipsae, quid plenum, quid inane sit judicant,: quod honestum nos et laudabile esse dicamus, id illi cassum quiddam et inani vocis sono decoratum esse dicant,; cf.: honesti inane nomen esse,: sin vera visa divina sunt, falsa autem et inania humana,: voces inanes fundere,; cf. elocutio,: damnatus inani judicio,: vox,: verba,; ; cf. verborum torrenti,: crimen,: o inanes nostras contentiones!: o spes fallaces et cogitationes inanes meae!; cf.: inani et tenui spe te consolaris,: spes,: religio,: delectari multis inanibus rebus, ut gloriā, etc.,; : cupiditates,: causas nequidquam nectis inanes,: minae,: tempus inane peto, requiem spatiumque furori,vacant, leisure,; so, ternpora (with morae),: tempora, in prosody, i. q. the Gr. κενὸς χρόνος,the use of a short syllable for a long one, Spald.—
With gen.: omnia plena consiliorum, inania verborum,poor in words,: quae inanissima prudentiae reperta sunt,.—
Of persons, vain, worthless, petty: Graii,: homo inanis et regiae superbiae,: imagines, quibus inanissimi homines serviunt,: inanes Hoc juvat,; ; : hi pressi et integri, contra inflati illi et inanes,; cf.: illud vero pusilli animi et inanis,: non negaverim totam Asiae regionem inaniora parere ingenia,.—
As subst.: ĭnāne, is, n., that which is empty or vain; emptiness, vanity, inanity: o curas hominum! o quantum est in rebus inane!: inane abscindere soldo,.— Plur.: dum vitat humum, nubes et inania captet,: inaina famae,idle reports,: inania belli,.—Hence, adv.: ĭnānĭter, vainly, idly, uselessly: exsultare,: moveri,; cf. : pectus angere,: medicas exercet inaniter artes,.

la:verb:inanio.html:
ĭnānĭo, īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4, v. a.
inanis
,
to make empty, to empty out, evacuate (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): hoc ubi inanitur spatium, etc.,; cf.: locus inanitus magis ac vacuatus,: herbacea arefacta per se inanit alvum,: vesicas (polium),: corpora (luna, opp. implet),.—Part. as subst.: ĭnānītum, i, n., vacancy, emptiness (opp. plenum), .
la:verb:inanio.inflection: īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4, v. a.

la:verb:inaudio.html:
ĭn-audĭo (arch. ind-audio, cf. Ritschl Proleg. ad ), īvi or ĭi, ītum, 4, v. a.,
to hear, learn, esp. something secret (mostly ante-class. and in the tempp. perff.): quod ego inaudivi, accipite, Pac. ap. : unde hoc tam repente jucundum inaudivi melum?: quorum erupit illa vox de qua ego ex te primum quiddam inaudieram,; cf.: numquid de quo inaudisti?: metus ne de hac re quippiam indaudiverit,; ; : nam os columnatum poëtae esse indaudivi barbaro,; ; : et Aquini et Fabrateriae consilia sunt inita de me quae te video inaudisse,; cf.: re denique multo ante Gadibus inaudita, fore huic ut ab illo periculum crearetur,: inaudita sententia,.—Absol.: bonis dictis, quaeso, ne ille inaudiat, Afran. ap. (Com. Rel. p. 149 Rib.).

la:verb:inambulo.gloss: to walk or pace up and down or to and fro
senses: to walk or pace up and down or to and fro
la:verb:inambulo.html:
ĭn-ambŭlo, āre, v. n.,
to walk up and down, pace to and fro (class.): paululum in porticu,: in viridi opacaque ripa,: domi,: cum quidam pransus ... manibus ad tergum rejectis inambularet, Asin. ap. : per muros,.— Impers.: inambulandumst,.

la:adj:inamabilis.html:
ĭn-ămābĭlis, e, adj.,
not worthy of love, not lovely, repugnant, revolting, hateful, odious (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): inamabilis, illepidus vivo,: genus ipsum inamabile, inamoenum,: tristique palus inamabilis undā,: regnum (of the Lower World),; : feritas,: nihil est inamabilius quam diligens stultitia, — In the neutr. adverb.: inamabile ridet,.

la:adj:inaccessus.html:
ĭn-accessus, a, um, adj.,
unapproached, unapproachable, inaccessible (cf.: invius, impervius, devius, avius).
Lit. (poet. and post-Aug.): mare scopulis inaccessum,: montes,; ; : aditus,: lucus,: spelunca radiis solis,.—
Trop., unattainable: Pindarus imitationi,: formositas,.

la:adj:inausus.html:
ĭn-ausus, a, um, adj.,
not ventured, unattempted (poet. and in post-Aug. prose): ne quid inausum Aut intractatum scelerisve dolive fuisset,: nefas,: quid enim per hosce dies inausum intemeratumve vobis?: sciat animus nihil inausum esse fortunae,med.—Plur. as subst.: ĭn-ausa, ōrum, n., unattempted things, deeds beyond daring: quae inausa audeat,.

la:other:Inachus.html:
Īnăchus or -os, i, m., = Ἴναχος,
the first king of Argos, father of Io and Phoroneus, ; ; ; . Also, a river in Argolis named for king Inachus, now Banitza, ; ; sq.; ; .—
Derivv.
īnăchĭus, a, um, adj., Inachian;poet. also, i. q. Argive or Grecian: juvenca,i. e. Io.; hence also: bos,i. e. Isis, identified with Io,: ira,i. e. of Juno against Io,: Argi (governed by Inachus, or on the river Inachus), : undae,i. e. of the river Inachus,; but also of the Lernean Sea (of Lerna, near Argos), : rex,i. e. Adrastus, king of Argos,: litus, i. e. Argolic or Grecian, : urbes,: natae,: Linus (as the son of the Argive Psamathe), (3, 4), 8: Perseus (as the son of the Argive Danaë),. —
īnă-chus, a, um, adj., the same: pubes,i. e. Grecian,. —
īnăchĭ-des, ae, m., a male descendant of Inachus; so Perseus (cf. in the preced.), ; Epaphus (as the son of Io), ; in plur., the Argives, . — īnăchis, ĭdis, f., Inachian; or subst., a female descendant of Inachus: ripae,i. e. of the river Inachus,: Acrisione (as the daughter of the Argive Danaë),.— Subst., of lo, (3, 31), 4; ; ; identified with Isis (v. above, under Inachius),.—In plur.: īnăchĭdes, um, female Argives, .

la:verb:inardesco.gloss: to kindle, catch fire, burn, glow
senses: to kindle, catch fire, burn, glow
la:verb:inardesco.html:
ĭn-ardesco, arsi, 3,
v. inch.n., to kindle, take fire, burn, glow (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: nubes Solis inardescit radiis,: arbusculae in igne ut ferrum inardescentes,: nec munus (i. e. vestis) umeris Herculis Inarsit aestuosius,: inardescunt genae,. —
Trop.: affectus omnis languescat necesse est, nisi voce, vultu, totius prope habitu corporis inardescat,: cupidine vindictae inardescere,: ut vidit juvenem, specie praesentis inarsit,.

la:other:Inarime.gloss: synonym of Aenāria (island and dormant volcano)
senses: synonym of Aenāria (island and dormant volcano)
la:other:Inarime.html:
Īnărĭmē, ēs, f., = εἰν Ἀρίμοις (Hom. Il. 2, 783),
an island in the Tyrrhene Sea, on the coast of Campania, now Ischia, ; Heyne; ; ; ; ; : Inarime a Graecis dicta Pithecusa,.

la:adj:inaestimabilis.gloss: that cannot be estimated or judged
senses: that cannot be estimated or judged
la:adj:inaestimabilis.html:
ĭn-aestĭmābĭlis, e, adj.
In gen., that cannot be estimated or judged of: nihil tam incertum nec tam inaestimabile est quam animi multitudinis,so little to be counted upon,. —
In partic.
Inestimable, invaluable, incalculable: quod e grege se imperatorum, velut inaestimabilem, secrevisset,: gaudium,: monumentum occasionis,. — *
Not worthy to be esteemed, valueless, opp. aestimabile, .

la:verb:inauro.html:
ĭn-auro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to cover or overlay with gold, to gild (class.; most freq. in the part. perf.).
Lit.: tegulas aereas,; : maurata statua,: columna extrinsecus,: Romulus (i. e. statua Romuli),: palla,: vestis,i. e. inwrought with gold,.—
Trop., to gild, i. e. to make rich: puto, te malle a Caesare consuli quam inaurari,: ut te Confestim liquidus fortunae rivus inauret,.— Hence. ĭnaurātus, a, um, P. a., gilded, golden: quis radat inaurati femur Herculis,.—Comp.: omni patagio inauratior pavo,

la:adj:inauditus.html:
ĭn-audītus, a, um, adj.,
unheard.
(On account of its novelty or strangeness.) Unheard-of, unusual, strange, new (freq. and class.; a favorite word of Cic.): nihil dicam reconditum, nihil aut inauditum vobis aut cuiquam novum,; cf. : quod nobis inauditum est,: novum est, non dico inusitatum, verum omnino inauditum,; cf. : novum crimen et ante hunc diem inauditum,: insignis quaedam, inaudita, nova magnitudo animi,: incredibilis atque inaudita gravitas,: modus et inauditus et incredibilis,: novellas et inauditas sectas veteribus religionibus opponere, Mos. et Rom. Leg. Coll. 15, 3, 3; cf. § 7.— Comp.: hominum nescias invisitatius an inauditius genus,.—
Unheard (of an accused person), without a hearing (only post-Aug.): inauditus et indefensus,; ; cf.: inauditos et innoxios relegavit,; ; ; ; also of the cause or defence of the accused: neque inaudita causa quemquam damnari, etc.,.—*
Without hearing: alia (animalia) gignuntur aut inodora inauditave, (al. inauritave).

la:noun:inanitas.html:
ĭnānĭtas, ātis, f.
inanis
.
Lit., emptiness, empty space (rare but class.): mihi inanitate Jamdudum intestina murmurant,: per inanitatem ferri,: oris,.—
Trop., emptiness, uselessness, inanity (rare but class.): amputata circumcisaque inanitate omni,; : verborum et imaginum,.

la:adj:inamissibilis.html:
ĭn-āmissĭbĭlis, e, adj.,
that cannot be lost (late Lat.): voluntas pietatis, , 22, 30 med.

la:adj:inanimus.html:
ĭnănĭmus, a, um, adj.
2. in-animus
,
lifeless, inanimate (class.; cf. Madv. ad ): cum inter inanimum et animal hoc maxime intersit, quod inanimum nihil agit, animal agit aliquid,; cf.: inanimum est omne, quod pulsu agitatur externo; quod autem est animal, id motu cietur interiore et suo,: cujusque generis vel inanimi vel animantis origo,; : res (opp. quodque animal),: natura,: muta atque inanima,; so with muta,; : omnes res, animantes et inanimae,; ; cf.: ex mutis animalibus aut inanimis,: satiati caede animantium, quae inanima erant, etc.,.

la:adj:inanimis.html:
ĭnănĭmis, e, adj.
2. in-anima
,
without breath or without life, breathless, lifeless, inanimate (Appuleian): ventus,i. e. that does not blow,: humi projectus, inanimis, p. 108, 25; cf. .

la:verb:inaestuo.html:
ĭn-aestŭo, āre, v. n.,
to boil or rage in any thing (rare): bilis,: succensi stomacho fellis inaestuans (impietas),, praef. 58.

la:adj:inanimatus.html:
ĭn-ănĭmātus, a, um, adj.,
lifeless, inanimate (late Lat.), Boëth. Arist. Anal. Prior. 1, 4, p. 471 sq. (but not in Cicero; v. Madv. ad ).

la:verb:inauguro.gloss: to divine, practice augury, take omens from the flight of birds
senses: to divine, practice augury, take omens from the flight of birds
to consecrate, inaugurate, approve on the basis of omens
la:verb:inauguro.html:
ĭn-augŭro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.
Lit.To take omens from the flight of birds, to practise augury, to divine: per sacram viam augures ex arce profecti solent inaugurare, Müll.: impetritum, inauguratum'st: quovis admittunt aves,: Palatinum Romulus, Aventinum Remus ad inaugurandum templa capiunt,: agedum, divine tu, inaugura, fierine possit, quod nunc ego mente concipio,. —Hence, b. inaugŭrāto, adv. (lit. abl. absol.), after consulting the birds: id quia inaugurato Romulus fecerat,: consecrare locum,.—
Transf.
To give a certain sanctity to a place or (official) person by ceremony of consulting the flight of birds, to consecrate, inaugurate, install: locum,: VRBEM (Romulus) Calend. Praenest. ap. : cur non inaugurare? Sume diem; vide, qui te inauguret,: augur in locum ejus inauguratus est filius,; so, aliquem flaminem,; .—
In gen., to install: cena et poculis magnis inauguratur (dux latronum),: comitia, quae habentur aut regis aut flaminum inaugurandorum causa, Lab. ap. : si flamines Diales inaugurentur,.
la:verb:inauguro.inflection: āvi, ātum, 1, v. n. and a.

la:noun:inambulatio.gloss: pacing up and down (especially of an orator on stage)
senses: pacing up and down (especially of an orator on stage)
la:noun:inambulatio.html:
ĭnambŭlātĭo, ōnis, f.
inambulo
.
A walking up and down on the rostra (of orators; rare but class.),; . — Poet.: tremuli lecti, a moving or shaking to and fro, .—
Transf., a place to walk in, a walk, promenade, ; .

la:noun:inaequalitas.html:
ĭnaequālĭtas, ātis, f.
2. in-aequalis
,
unevenness, unlikeness, inequality (not in Cic.).
In gen.: togae et tunicae, Müll.: inaequalitate dissident (supercilia),: coloris,; .—In plur., ; .—
In partic., grammatical irregularity, anomaly, Müll.; .

la:verb:inaedifico.gloss: to build in, on, at or up, erect
senses: to build in, on, at or up, erect
la:verb:inaedifico.html:
ĭn-aedĭfĭco, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to build in, on, or at a place; to build up, erect.
Lit. (class.): neiquis in ieis loceis ... quid inaedificatum inmolitumve habeto, Lex. Jul. Munic. 71: inaedificata in muris moenia,: de domo tua, in qua ita est inaedificatum sacellum, ut, etc.,; : conjectis celeriter stramentis (tecta) inaedificare,: quae in loca publica inaedificata habebant,: tribus primis et quinto aquilarum generi inaedificatur nido lapis aëtites,is built into, made a part of,: supra pilas, (al. aedificare).— Poet.: nisi inaedificata superne multa forent multis nubila,piled upon,. —
Transf.
To build up, wall up: portas obstruit, vicos plateasque inaedificat,: nec clausae modo portae, sed etiam inaedificatae erant,; cf.: a Serrano sanctissima sacella suffossa, inaedificata, oppressa ... foedata esse nescimus?.—
To build upon, to cover with buildings: aliquem locum,—
Trop., to burden: quantum imponere et, ut ita dicam, inaedificare voluisset,.

la:verb:inaequo.gloss: to make equal, level or even
senses: to make equal, level or even
la:verb:inaequo.html:
ĭn-aequo, āre, v. a.,
to make even or level: haec levibus cratibus terraque inaequat,.

la:adj:inauspicatus.html:
ĭn-auspĭcātus, a, um, adj.
At which no auspices were taken, without auspices: lex,.—Hence,
in-auspĭcāto, adv. (lit. abl. absol.), without consulting the auspices: quod inauspicato pomoerium transgressus esset (Ti. Gracchus),.—
Of bad omen, unlucky, inauspicious (only post-Aug.): inauspicatarum animantium vice,: nomen,: exemplum,: garrulitas (cornicis),: bibente conviva mensam tolli inauspicatissimum judicatur,.—
Unhoped for, unexpected (late Lat.): successus,: bona,.
